patients.summary: Healthy 32-year-old teacher with two prior term vaginal births who joins the practice in September 2025 while trying to conceive. Her third pregnancy is complicated by complete placenta previa at 20 weeks and severe fetal anemia from fetomaternal hemorrhage at 30 weeks treated with intrauterine transfusion, and ends in intrauterine fetal demise at 36 weeks with cesarean delivery. The chart follows her postpartum recovery and grief in primary care.

events.reason: New patient, establish care and physical

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient. 32 yo elementary school teacher, moved her care here from a practice she used for years; wanted something where she can actually reach a doctor. Two kids at home.

No chronic medical problems. No surgeries. No hospitalizations aside from deliveries.

OB hx: G2P2002. Both pregnancies uneventful, both vaginal deliveries at term.

She and her husband are hoping to have a third. Has been on a prenatal vitamin daily for a couple of months for that reason. LMP 8/26, cycles regular. No pelvic pain or abnormal bleeding.

Meds: prenatal vitamin 1 tab daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: teaches 2nd grade. Never smoked. A glass of wine now and then, stopped since they started trying. No drug use. Exercises by walking.
FH: nothing she knows of.

Last Pap: thinks 2023, normal. Will get records.
Vaccines: childhood series complete per pt; flu shots most years.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities no edema. Skin no rashes. Mood and affect normal. PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Preventive care, new patient. CBC, CMP, lipids today. Records request sent to prior practice. Pap due 2028 if 2023 co-test confirmed normal.
2. Preconception. Continue prenatal vitamin. No alcohol once trying in earnest. Let me know when she has a positive test and I'll get her to OB.
3. Flu and COVID this fall, both fine in pregnancy. Can do at a nurse visit next month.

Return in a year for physical, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Alyssa, your blood work from Wednesday is all normal: blood count, kidney and liver tests, and sugar. LDL cholesterol is 106, a hair over the lab's optimal cutoff and nothing to treat at your age. Nothing to do. Nice to meet you this week.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care practice

documents.title: Prior Practice Records Summary
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received from patient's previous primary care office, 41 pages, scanned to media.

Abstracted:
- Cervical cytology with HPV co-test, 2023: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, high-risk HPV not detected.
- No chronic problems on their list. No medications other than a prenatal vitamin.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Immunizations: childhood series documented; Tdap with each prior pregnancy; seasonal flu most years.
- No prior surgeries.

Forwarded to PCP to review.

documents.title: Positive test!
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning! Two home tests this morning, both positive. First day of my last period was August 26. Feeling fine so far, a little tired. What do I do next? I'd like to go back to the OB group I used last time if they take referrals from you.

documents.title: RE: Positive test!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! By your period you're about 5 1/2 weeks, which puts your due date around June 2. I've sent the referral to the OB group so they can set up your first prenatal visit, usually around 8 weeks. Keep taking the prenatal vitamin, skip alcohol, and call them or us for heavy bleeding or bad cramping. We'll still do your flu and COVID shots here this month.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt here after school for vaccines. Currently about 7 weeks pregnant, first OB appt next week. Screening questions reviewed, no fever today, no prior vaccine reactions.

Influenza (trivalent) 0.5 mL IM R deltoid.
COVID-19 updated formula 0.3 mL IM L deltoid.

VIS given for both. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Pt left ambulatory.

documents.title: Obstetrics - New Prenatal Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
RE: Alyssa Krause, DOB 11/30/1992
Visit date: 10/21/2025

Thank you for the referral. Mrs. Krause was seen today to begin prenatal care for her third pregnancy. She is G3P2002; both earlier pregnancies ended in uncomplicated vaginal births at term.

She feels well with mild fatigue and occasional nausea. No bleeding or pain. LMP 8/26/2025.

Dating ultrasound: single intrauterine pregnancy, cardiac activity present, crown-rump length consistent with dates at 8w0d. EDD 6/2/2026 by LMP, confirmed by ultrasound.

Prenatal laboratory results:
- Blood type A, Rh(D) positive; antibody screen negative
- Rubella immune; varicella immune
- Hepatitis B surface antigen negative
- HIV negative
- Hepatitis C antibody negative
- Syphilis screen nonreactive
- Urine culture negative
- Hemoglobin within normal limits

Blood pressure normal today.

Medications: prenatal vitamin daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Plan: routine prenatal visits; anatomy ultrasound at 20 weeks; glucose screening at 24 to 28 weeks. We see that she has had influenza and COVID vaccines this season.

Sincerely,
Obstetrics & Gynecology
